S14b: the run emitter (codeagent/emitter.py) -- numbered, stored, delivered server events.

Three layers of tests, all against in-memory twins behind the real interfaces (the run
store, the encrypted Redis buffer and run_guard's Redis from tests/unit/run_manager_testkit.py,
the real protocol/v1 validator):

  * unit tests with a stand-in connection in an in-memory registry (what one emit does:
    number, store, deliver, in that order; what it refuses; the per-run lock; verbatim
    re-delivery; the terminal event that has no buffer to number it from);
  * the same claims through S04's real socket (tests/unit/codeagent_testkit.Rig), with every
    frame the device receives checked against protocol/v1, so "valid envelope", "contiguous
    seq" and "the resumed device gets exactly what it missed" are proven on the transport;
  * content hygiene: a canary in an event's text and in a Redis fault never reaches the log.

Maps to the work package ("What" 2 and "Content hygiene" 5):

  * sequence, storage and delivery are atomic per run ..................... test_concurrent_*, test_exclusive_*
  * emit_state_changed(run_id, state, reason=None) ........................ test_emit_state_changed_*
  * re-delivery is verbatim and i

Patch S07b -- unit tests for leaving plan mode (codeagent/loop.py and runs.set_mode).

THE GAP THESE TESTS PIN. A run's mode reaches the server once, in run.start. In plan mode the loop shows the model
only the read-only tools plus plan_exit. When the person approves plan_exit the DEVICE leaves plan mode and answers
the call with a successful tool_result; the server was never told, so the model stayed read-only for the rest of the
run. S07b makes the loop switch the run to `ask` when (and only when) an OK plan_exit comes back for a run that is in
plan mode, and STORE the new mode in the run row (the buffer's state is sealed once, so a resume reads the row).

Groups: runs.set_mode itself (over the in-memory run store), the switch inside a turn, every case that must leave
the mode alone, the switch surviving a resume, and the log. The run, its buffer, run_manager and run_guard are the
REAL S06 modules over their in-memory twins (the same Rig the S07 tests use); the model is scripted and the broker
is a recording fake.

Patch S07 -- unit tests for codeagent/loop.py (the agent loop executor v0).

A scripted fake model drives the loop; the run, its buffer, run_manager and run_guard are the REAL S06/eo modules
over their in-memory twins (run_manager_testkit.World); the broker is a recording fake except in the tests that
name the real one. Groups: the step, tool calls, malformed calls, plan mode, approvals, cancel, limits and
breakers, provider fallback, metering, disconnect/pause/resume, logging, wiring.

Patch S15 -- the loop's one additive change: tools are offered only to a connection that can answer them.

The device says what it can do in `hello.capabilities`; the server keeps that on the connection. S15's wiring
gives the loop a small predicate (`offer_tools(conn) -> bool`); the loop asks it once per turn and, when the answer
is no, offers NO tools to the model and refuses any call the model makes anyway, so that a `tool_proposed` is never
sent to a client that cannot answer it. These tests drive the loop alone (the scripted model, the real S06
modules over their in-memory twins, a recording broker); tests/unit/test_codeagent_wiring_flow.py drives the same
rule through the real router, run handlers and broker.

  * no predicate (the default): exactly what S07 did, every visible tool is offered ........ test_default_*
  * predicate says no: no tools in the request, the reply still streams .................... test_no_tools_*
  * a call the model makes anyway: never forwarded, answered with a fixed text ............ test_a_call_*
  * the predicate is given the turn's connection and asked once per turn ................... test_predicate_*
  * a predicate that raises: no tools (fail closed), the type is logged, never the text ..... test_a_failing_*
  * plan mode and the gate compose: the gate can only remove tools, never widen them ....... test_plan_mode_*

S04b: in a backend install, the device socket's protocol reader loads.

codeagent/ws.py validates every message with protocol/validate.py, which needs
jsonschema (and `referencing`) and the protocol/v1 schemas. Until S04b a backend
install only got jsonschema transitively (guardrails-ai, litellm) and the container
had no protocol/ directory, so load_protocol() raised ProtocolUnavailable there and the
socket failed closed.

This file is the other half of tests/static/test_protocol_runtime.py (which reads the
requirements files, the Dockerfile and the dev overlay as text): it proves that in the
environment `pip install -r backend/requirements.txt` builds, the production loader
really works. It is deliberately NOT guarded by pytest.importorskip("jsonschema"): a
backend install that lacks jsonschema is exactly the regression to catch, so it must
fail here rather than skip. It lives in tests/unit because CI's backend job runs
`pytest tests/unit tests/integration` and does not collect tests/static.

The image and the dev overlay are checked by hand with the commands in the S04b patch
description (docker build, then `python -c "from codeagent.ws import load_protocol; ..."`).

S14c: the run handlers' base (codeagent/run_handlers.py) -- the ownership guard, the error
map, the hook registries, `run.start`, and the disconnect handler.

Everything runs against the in-memory twins behind the real interfaces (run store, encrypted
Redis buffer, run_guard's Redis; tests/unit/run_manager_testkit.World) and the REAL protocol/v1
validator. Two layers:

  * unit tests call the handlers directly with a stand-in connection that records what it was
    sent (frames and errors) and sits in an in-memory registry, so "the device got seq 1 and 2"
    and "the registry holds a newer connection" are exact;
  * socket tests go through S04's real endpoint (tests/unit/codeagent_testkit.Rig) with the
    real MessageRouter, every frame the device receives checked against protocol/v1: a run is
    started over the wire, the device leaves, and the run is paused with the pause in its
    replay; a reconnect does NOT pause its own run.

Maps to the work package ("What" 3, first and last bullets, and 4, 5):
  * every handler first checks the run belongs to this user AND device; anything else is
    run_not_found and never reveals whether the run exists .......... test_guard_*
  * S06's errors are mapped with run_manager's table ................... test_error_map_*
  * run.start: start_run, a parallel-run cap that tests can inject, created -> running, the
    state_changed events (seq 1, 2) ...................................... test_run_start_*
  * on_disconnect: run-disconnect
